result.summary:
Completed the "文献员" (literature officer) role for C05 seed 805, round 1.

What I did:
1. Read /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C05/partura/s805/r1/analysis.md (the structural-dissection output from round 1), which ends with four literature questions (L1–L4) all targeting the core `day_centroid(Volume)` (intraday volume-timing centroid) found in M's batch 1, plus loc.md and PLAN.md for context. Grepped partura/ops_ext.py and AlphaCube-steering's operator source to confirm every operator name I used in the write-up (day_centroid, day_signed_ratio, day_gini, day_at_max_ratio, day_argmax, cross_zscore, cross_madz, cs_bucket_rank, cross_corr, cross_regres, cs_flip_by_state, day_wmean, etc.) actually exists — none invented.
2. Loaded WebSearch/WebFetch via ToolSearch and ran ~25 searches (plus a few WebFetch/Crossref lookups to pin down exact publication dates) covering: intraday volume U-shape/timing literature, China closing-call-auction reform and passive/ETF ownership link to auction volume, own-history (abnormal) volume vs cross-sectional turnover-level literature, intraday momentum / "smart money" / order-imbalance construction, and A-share limit-up/limit-down and institutional-vs-retail intraday timing evidence.
3. Enforced the pre-2023-08-08 cutoff strictly: verified exact dates via Crossref API for the two border-line journal articles (Han et al., Pacific-Basin Finance Journal, confirmed 2022-09; Qiu, Huang & Jiang, Finance Research Letters, confirmed 2023-06 — both safely before cutoff), and explicitly excluded/flagged sources whose date I could not pin down (a 2025 arXiv intraday-volume-forecasting paper was excluded outright as post-cutoff; a DISIA working paper and an NUS working paper are flagged "date unconfirmed, not used as dated evidence").
4. Wrote /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C05/partura/s805/r1/lit.md: for each of L1–L4, listed concrete processing recipes translated into this environment's operator language (e.g. `cross_zscore(day_centroid(Volume), d)` for own-history standardization per Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin 2001 vs Datar-Naik-Radcliffe 1998's raw cross-sectional level ranking; `cs_bucket_rank(day_centroid(Volume), LogFloatCap)` per Bogousslavsky-Muravyev's ETF/passive-ownership-vs-market-cap nonlinearity finding and Qiu-Huang-Jiang 2023's China-specific institution-trades-more-at-open/close evidence; `day_signed_ratio(Ret, Amt)` per Chordia-Roll-Subrahmanyam 2002 order-imbalance and the Pastor-Stambaugh 2003 return-signed-volume proxy; open/close-half-hour interaction per Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 2018's "Market Intraday Momentum"), each tagged to a numbered source. Ended with a full 15-row source table (title/authors/year-month/venue/link/verified true-or-false) and an explicit "what literature does NOT support" section (no paper found testing a single intraday-volume-centroid scalar as a cross-sectional factor directly; no A-share-specific study tying tail-of-day volume share to index/ETF/institutional ownership with a concrete stripping method; no literature-based window choice for 20/60/250-day standardization; no sell-side "smart money" report text, only an academic proxy; no literature on limit-up/limit-down exclusion rules for this kind of feature). Reported several negative-search results honestly rather than guessing, per the task's explicit "搜不到就写搜不到,不得编造" instruction.

Compliance: did not run any server, did not modify code/PLAN/any other seed's files, did not git commit, only wrote the one file this role is responsible for (s805/r1/lit.md). Read only s805/r1/{analysis.md,loc.md}, PLAN.md, and operator source code, consistent with this role's read allowlist.

Note: unrelated files elsewhere in the repo (scripts/c05_sync.sh, handoff/workflows/*, runs/_risk/*, logs/_wf_dump.log) show as modified/untracked in git status — these are from the concurrent orchestration (M's GP batches and other seeds/agents running in parallel), not from anything I touched.
